content.answer: Fix: open(path, encoding='utf-8').read() (or open the file in binary and decode the bytes as UTF-8); never rely on the platform default encoding, which is ASCII in the C locale, GBK on Chinese Windows, etc., and will crash with UnicodeDecodeError or mojibake CJK/emoji text.
content.reuse_advice: At every text-input boundary — reading files, subprocess output, sockets, or environment strings — always pass encoding='utf-8' explicitly (plus errors= policy if needed), or read bytes and decode as UTF-8 yourself; never depend on locale.getpreferredencoding() or the platform default, since it varies (C/POSIX=ASCII, Windows legacy=GBK/cp1252) and causes UnicodeDecodeError or silent mojibake for non-ASCII text.
